newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian guru conjures up gold chain for Fergie.
newsitem.headline: Indian guru conjures up gold chain for Fergie.

text.p: An Indian guru produced a gold chain and cross, apparently out of thin air, and gave it to visiting British royal Sarah Ferguson, a holistic healer who brought her to India said on Saturday.
Dr Isaac Mathai, a homoeopath treating the Duchess of York, told Reuters in the southern city of Bangalore that the event happened during her meeting with Sai Baba in the nearby town of Puttaparthi.

Asked if the guru, who is often said by his followers to conjure up gifts from nowhere, produced anything for the duchess, Mathai said: "Lots of vibhuti (sacred ash). And she got a gold chain with a cross.
"That proves he (Sai Baba) believes in all religions."
Sai Baba, who wears long orange robes and sports an Afro hairdo, counts among his followers the former Indian prime minister, P.V. Narasimha Rao.
The duchess stepped out of her Bangalore hotel wearing an Indian "salwar-kameez" -- a loose, long shirt and baggy trousers -- and declared she planned to practise homeopathy.
"I am interested in homeopathy. I will be practising homeopathy," she told waiting reporters before speeding off. She was on her way to Bombay, a staff member of her hotel said.
Ferguson, known as "Fergie" to Britain's tabloid press, is making a personal trip to India. She was accompanied by Mathai and his wife on Saturday.
"The visit to Puttaparthi went off very well. She is really enjoying herself," Mathai said.
Puttaparthi is 150 km (95 miles) from Bangalore in the neighbouring state of Andhra Pradesh.

In the United States earlier this month, the duchess signed high-priced deals to advertise cranberry juice on television and be a spokeswoman for Weight Watchers International, the programme she credited for helping her slim down.
